title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity and mortality in calcific aortic valve stenosis: the ARISTOTLE cohort study
authors: Jiayuan Zhang; Ziwei Zhou; Xinghao Xu; Yue Guo; Zhenyu Xiong; Menghui Liu; Shaozhao Zhang; Rihua Huang; Han Wen; Yiqi Zheng; Xinyuan Chen; Longyun Peng; Xiaodong Zhuang; Xinxue Liao
abstract: Abstract Background Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM), defined as the coexistence of two or more cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), is highly prevalent in patients with calcific aortic valve stenosis (CAVS). However, its association with mortality in this population remains poorly characterized. Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed 1175 adults with echocardiographically confirmed CAVS from the ARISTOTLE (Aortic valve diseases RISk facTOr assessmenT and prognosis modeL construction) registry. Participants were stratified by baseline CMD count into pre-specified primary exposure groups: CMM0 (no CMD), CMM1 (one CMD), and CMM2–3 (≥ 2 CMDs). CMDs included type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), coronary heart disease (CHD), and ischemic stroke. Cause-specific Cox proportional-hazards models were applied; non-cardiovascular deaths were treated as censoring events for cardiovascular mortality analyses. Fine–Gray competing-risk models were constructed, with non-cardiovascular death set as the competing event. Formal interaction testing with Bonferroni correction was conducted for pre-defined subgroup analyses. Exploratory four-category CMD stratification and analyses of distinct CMD combinations were presented in supplementary materials. Results During a median follow-up of 3.23 years, 329 all-cause deaths and 179 cardiovascular deaths occurred. Mortality risk tended to increase with higher cardiometabolic multimorbidity burden. In the fully adjusted model, participants with ≥ 2 CMDs showed higher risk of all-cause mortality (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.23–2.48; P = 0.002) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 2.24, 95% CI 1.39–3.61; P < 0.001), compared with patients without CMD. Each incremental rise in CMD count was associated with 30% higher all-cause death risk (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10–1.53, P = 0.002) and 47% higher cardiovascular death risk (HR 1.47, 95% CI 1.18–1.84, P < 0.001). Fine–Gray competing-risk analyses yielded consistent findings (subdistribution HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.30–3.28, P = 0.002 for CMM2–3 versus CMM0). Associations between CMD burden and mortality were directionally uniform across most predefined subgroups; no statistically significant interaction remained after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusions Among patients with calcific aortic valve stenosis, higher cumulative cardiometabolic multimorbidity burden was independently associated with elevated all‑cause and cardiovascular mortality. These observational findings suggest that assessment of cumulative cardiometabolic comorbidity burden may add prognostic context for patients with CAVS.

title: False patency, true occlusion: perfusion imaging and dual stent-retriever thrombectomy for a calcified carotid terminus embolus
authors: Mingzhu Huang; Shujuan Gan; Jinfeng Miao; Ruihan Zhu; Jintao Chen; Wenhuo Chen
abstract: Calcified cerebral emboli are an uncommon cause of acute ischemic stroke and may produce a false-patency sign on computed tomography angiography because their high attenuation can mimic intravascular contrast material. We report the case of a 77-year-old woman who presented with a wake-up stroke approximately 14 hours after she was last known well, with right hemiplegia and global aphasia. Noncontrast computed tomography showed a markedly hyperattenuating intraluminal focus at the left carotid terminus and proximal M1 segment, suggesting a calcified cerebral embolus. Computed tomography angiography appeared to show severe stenosis with residual luminal patency, whereas computed tomography perfusion demonstrated extensive hypoperfusion involving the left middle cerebral artery and bilateral anterior cerebral artery territories. Because the severe neurologic deficit and perfusion abnormality were discordant with the apparent patency on computed tomography angiography, cerebral angiography was performed. Digital subtraction angiography demonstrated complete occlusion of the left M1 origin and near-complete occlusion of the left A1 segment; the right A1 segment was congenitally hypoplastic. A rigid calcified embolus spanning the carotid-terminus bifurcation was retrieved using a balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent technique under proximal flow arrest, achieving complete reperfusion in a single pass. Histopathologic examination confirmed calcified embolic material. This case highlights the value of multimodal imaging and confirmatory angiography when clinical and imaging findings are discordant. In this patient, balloon guide catheter-assisted dual-stent retrieval was a tailored and feasible strategy; however, a single case cannot establish its superiority over other thrombectomy approaches.

title: Association Between Changes in Paravalvular Leakage After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase
authors: Akihiro Ikuta; Gakuto Bando; Satoki Oka; Shunsuke Matsushita; Naoya Inoue; Shingo Hirao; Mitsuru Abe; Kazushige Kadota; Tatsuhiko Komiya; Yasushi Fuku
abstract: Background: The association between changes in paravalvular leakage (PVL) and serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is unexplored. We aimed to investigate the short-term changes in PVL after TAVI and their association with LDH elevation. Methods: A total of 550 consecutive patients underwent TAVI from 2020 to 2024. Of these, 313 receiving SAPIEN 3 (S3) or SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR) valves were included in this study. Patients were categorized into two groups based on whether their PVL severity worsened by at least one grade from immediately after the procedure to hospital discharge. Results: PVL deterioration was observed in 16.3% of patients. The incidence of moderate or greater LDH elevation was significantly higher in the PVL deterioration group than in the non-PVL deterioration group at 7 days (17.6% vs. 8.4%; P = 0.04) and 1 month (29.4% vs. 8.8%; P < 0.01) after the procedure. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for predicting PVL deterioration using the sizing index (SI) was 0.84, with an optimal cut-off value of 96.5% (odds ratio (OR): 13.6; 95% confidence interval (CI): 6.55–31.1; P < 0.01). Multivariable analysis showed that an aortic valve calcium score ≥ 1,435, use of the S3UR valve, and an SI < 96.5 were independently associated with PVL deterioration. Conclusion: Early PVL deterioration after TAVI with a balloon-expandable valve may be associated with LDH elevation. These findings highlight the importance of selecting a prosthetic valve with an appropriate sizing ratio to minimize PVL deterioration after TAVI.

title: Head-to-head comparison of complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices for predicting 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve implantation
authors: Hakan İskender; Ömer  Abdulbaki Kılıç; Batıkan Hafızoğlu; M. Bahadır Omar; Süleyman Çağan Efe
abstract: Several complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices have been proposed for risk stratification after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but their relative prognostic value remains uncertain. We compared preprocedural and early postprocedural indices to identify the most informative marker for 1-year outcomes. This retrospective single-center study included 413 patients undergoing transfemoral TAVI in 2023. Preprocedural indices were available for all patients and postprocedural indices within 24 h for 407. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality; the secondary endpoint was all-cause readmission within 1 year after discharge from the index TAVI hospitalization. Mortality discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis, and independent associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was further assessed using calibration, internal bootstrap validation, and decision curve analysis. During 1-year follow-up, 85 patients (20.6%) died. Among 407 patients with complete early postprocedural blood counts, postprocedural neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) showed the highest discrimination for mortality (AUC 0.746, 95% CI 0.678–0.808). In the fully adjusted model, postprocedural NLR remained independently associated with mortality (adjusted OR 2.65, 95% CI 1.96–3.60; P < 0.001), whereas no composite index showed a higher AUC. The final model achieved an AUC of 0.787. Hospitalization discrimination was modest. Early postprocedural NLR showed the highest discriminatory performance for 1-year mortality among routinely available hematologic inflammatory indices after TAVI. Its simplicity and availability suggest potential utility as an adjunctive marker for early postprocedural risk stratification. Not applicable. Not applicable.

title: Virtual Assessment of Coronary Microcirculation Before and After Rotational Atherectomy
authors: Gueladio Koné; Brahim Baala; Alexandre Canville; Matthieu Godin; Quentin Landolff
abstract: Background: Calcified coronary lesions remain a major challenge during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Rotational atherectomy (RA) (Boston Scientific) is a well-established tool used to modify calcified plaques and facilitate stent delivery. Despite its mechanical benefits, RA may adversely affect coronary microcirculation through distal plaque debris embolization. Angiography-derived microvascular resistance (AMR) (Pulse Medical) is a wire-free index correlated with invasive indices such as the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR), which allows assessment of microcirculatory resistance directly from angiographic images, without a pressure wire or adenosine. The objective of this study is to evaluate changes in AMR before and after RA and to identify clinical, angiographic, and procedural predictors of postprocedural coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD). Methods: We performed a retrospective single-center observational study including all patients who underwent RA between January 2023 and December 2024 at Clinique Saint-Hilaire in Rouen, France. AMR was measured before and after RA using the AngioPlus software (Pulse Medical). CMD was defined as postprocedural AMR > 250 mm Hg·s/m. Results: Of 49 RA procedures, 40 patients were included. AMR increased in all cases but CMD occurred in 42.5% of patients (n=17). Diabetes mellitus and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were significantly more prevalent in the CMD group. Long coronary artery lesions (> 20 mm), larger plaque burden, and prolonged burr run time were associated with higher AMR values. Mean AMR rose from 176 to 315 mm Hg·s/m in the CMD group, versus 177 to 201 mm Hg·s/m in the non-CMD group. Conclusions: Performing RA affects the coronary microcirculation, especially in cases of diabetes mellitus and reduced LVEF.

title: Beyond the usual: coronary artery abnormalities in Noonan syndrome
authors: Bilgehan Betül Biçer; Hayrettin Hakan Aykan; Ercan Tutar
abstract: Background. Noonan syndrome (NS) is a multisystemic genetic disorder primarily affecting the cardiovascular system. While pulmonary valve stenosis and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are common cardiac manifestations, coronary artery anomalies (CAAs) are rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Case Presentation. A 12-year-old boy with genetically confirmed Noonan syndrome due to a PTPN11 mutation (p.Asn308Asp, c.922A>G) had been followed since infancy. He initially had mild pulmonary valve stenosis that regressed spontaneously. He received intermittent growth hormone therapy, which was discontinued for two years and restarted 1.5 years prior to presentation. Routine echocardiography revealed newly detected coronary artery ectasia involving the left main coronary artery (LMCA) and the left anterior descending (LAD) artery. Coronary computed tomography angiography confirmed ectatic dilation of the LMCA and LAD, with an intramyocardial course of the mid-LAD. Further evaluation with cardiopulmonary exercise testing, myocardial perfusion scintigraphy, and selective coronary angiography demonstrated normal myocardial perfusion, an absence of ischemia, and diffuse coronary ectasia without discrete aneurysm formation. The patient remained asymptomatic, and no flow-limiting lesions were identified. Conclusion. This case highlights a rare vascular manifestation of NS and underscores the importance of vigilant cardiovascular surveillance. Due to the rarity of such cases and the lack of standardized monitoring or treatment protocols, individualized risk stratification remains essential. Reporting such cases is critical for raising awareness and guiding future management strategies for coronary anomalies in Noonan syndrome.

title: Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Using the Self-Expanding Allegra Valve in Daily Practice
authors: Justina Zemaite; Stefan Erler; Ulrich Schäfer; Steffen Vormfelde; Bjoern Andrew Remppis; Katja Bohmann; Barbara Maria Januszewski; Christof Burgdorf
abstract: Background: Limited data are available of the self-expanding Allegra transcatheter heart valve (THV). The aim of this study was to investigate the safety and outcome of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) using the Allegra THV in daily practice. Methods: Between February 2018 and September 2024, 142 consecutive patients underwent Allegra TAVI at the Heart and Vascular Center, Bad Bevensen, Germany, either for native aortic stenosis (AS) (n = 117, median 82 (interquartile range 80–86) years) or degenerated aortic bioprostheses (n = 25, 80 (73–84) years) as valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Endpoints were defined according to Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 criteria. Results: The logistic EuroSCORE II was significantly higher in the cohort of patients with degenerated aortic bioprostheses than in those with native AS (14.4% (6.6–25.3%) versus 3.3% (2.5–5.7%), P < 0.01). Technical success was nearly identical in both cohorts (91.5% of patients with native AS and 92.0% of patients with ViV TAVI). Postinterventional aortic regurgitation ≥ moderate was found in 4.5% of patients with native AS and was not present in any patient with ViV TAVI. In the native AS cohort, mean and maximal aortic pressure gradients decreased from 44 (36–54) mm Hg and 72 (60–87) mm Hg before the intervention to 6 (5–9) mm Hg and 12 (9–15) mm Hg after Allegra TAVI. In the ViV cohort, mean and maximal transvalvular pressure gradients decreased from 34 (27–43) mm Hg and 59 (44–70) mm Hg to 9 (7–11) mm Hg and 16 (14–23) mm Hg, respectively. Periprocedural mortality rates (≤ 30 days) were 6.8% and 12.0% in the native AS and ViV cohorts, respectively. One-year and 3-year survival rates were 87.2% and 73.2% in the native AS cohort and 89.8% and 75.1% in the ViV cohort, respectively. Conclusions: TAVI using the self-expanding Allegra THV system is safe and leads to acute hemodynamic improvements in patients with native AS or degenerated aortic bioprostheses.

title: Suspected Syphilitic Left Main Coronary Ostial Stenosis Evaluated by Intravascular Ultrasound and Directional Coronary Atherectomy: A Case Report
authors: Yoshichika Miyazaki; Takafumi Nishimura; Masayuki Aoyama; Munehisa Sakamoto; Takumi Toya
abstract: A 49-year-old previously healthy man developed cardiopulmonary arrest during exercise caused by critical isolated left main coronary ostial stenosis.Positive syphilis serology and multimodality imaging suggested nonatherosclerotic vasculopathy.Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) demonstrated a predominantly fibrous lesion with minimal lipid or calcification.Directional coronary atherectomy (DCA) was performed before stenting to obtain tissue for histopathologic evaluation, which revealed fibrous intimal thickening without features of atherosclerotic plaque.Alternative inflammatory and systemic vasculopathies were excluded.Although definitive histopathologic confirmation of syphilitic arteritis was unavailable, the integrated clinical findings supported this diagnosis and illustrate the value of tissue characterization in atypical coronary lesions.

title: Digoxin Revisited: An Updated Review in the Light of Recent Trials
authors: Muhammad Saad; Muhammad Abdullah; Ankit Yelamarthy; Krystal John; Abbas Hayat Mallick; Behram Khan; Hassan Tahir; Rajan Krishnamani
abstract: Isolated from Digitalis species following William Withering’s 1785 work on foxglove, digoxin inhibits myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium and vagal tone to produce inotropic, rate-controlling, and neurohormonal-deactivating effects. The foundational DIG trial (1997) showed no mortality benefit but reduced heart failure hospitalizations, prompting a progressive guideline downgrade. Three decades later, DIGIT-HF (2025, digitoxin) and DECISION (2026, low dose digoxin) retested cardiac glycosides atop modern four pillar guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). DIGIT-HF significantly reduced the composite of death or worsening heart failure (hazard ratio (HR), 0.82), while DECISION showed a numerical but nonsignificant benefit. A pooled meta-analysis of DIG, DIGIT-HF, and DECISION (9,013 patients) confirmed a consistent 15% reduction in worsening heart failure events across three decades of changing background therapy, without a significant mortality effect. The Dig-RHD trial addressed an unstudied population: symptomatic rheumatic heart disease (RHD), a chronic valvular heart disease that results from permanent damage to cardiac valves due to group A streptococcal infection. RHD affects roughly 40 million people and causes approximately 300,000 deaths annually, disproportionately in low- and middle-income countries. In 1,769 patients randomized across 12 Indian centers, digoxin significantly reduced the composite of death or new-onset/worsening heart failure (31.4% vs. 35.5%; HR, 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.70 to 0.97; P = 0.02), with greater benefit in atrial fibrillation, women, and patients with low body mass index (BMI), and a number needed to treat of approximately 14 over 2 years. Digoxin is not a mortality-reducing drug, but pooled contemporary evidence establishes it as a reproducible, low-cost tool for reducing heart failure events, now supported for the first time by high-quality randomized data in RHD, a population with substantial global burden and no prior evidence-based medical therapy. These findings warrant reconsideration of digoxin’s guideline status and development of RHD-specific recommendations.

title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial
authors: Andrea Necchi; Chiara Mercinelli; Brigida Anna Maiorano; Michela Piacentini; Antonio Cigliola; Roberto Iacovelli; Chiara Ciccarese; Chiara Ligato; Patrizia Giannatempo; Alessandro Rametta; Paolo Gontero; Francesco Soria; Christine Schuberth-Wagner; Jörg Wischhusen; Bernhard Rössler; Michael Metterlein; Stefan Ries; Thorsten Ross; Aasim Amin; Tobias Dreker; Frank Hermann; Lena Lemke; Kathrin Klar; Olga Mitina; Ana Gjorgjioska; Petra Fettes; Alexandra Auckenthaler; Sujata Rao; Eugen Leo; Felix Sebastian Lichtenegger
abstract: Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) is overexpressed in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and was recently identified as a potential therapeutic target to overcome resistance to programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death ligand 1 (PDL1) blockade. We investigated the safety and efficacy of GDF-15 blockade in an exploratory, stratified, placebo-controlled, single-blinded, nonrandomized phase 2a trial (GDFATHER-NEO). Thirty-one cisplatin-ineligible or cisplatin-refusing patients with newly diagnosed MIBC (clinical T2–T4aN0M0) were stratified by tumor stage and PDL1 combined positive score (CPS) and allocated sequentially to receive three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab (N, 480 mg 4-weekly) plus the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab (V, 20 mg kg−1 4-weekly; n = 16) or placebo (P, n = 15), followed by radical cystectomy or repeat transurethral resection of the bladder tumor. Locally assessed pathologic complete response (pCR, ypT0N0/x) and Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1-based radiographic response served as dual primary endpoints. pCR was 33% (5 of 15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 12–62%) in patients receiving N + V versus 8% (1 of 13, 95% CI 0–36%) for N + P; major pathologic response was 60% (95% CI 32–84%) versus 23% (95% CI 5–54%), and radiographic overall response rate was 60% (95% CI 32–84%) versus 15% (95% CI 2–45%), respectively. Responses to N + V were associated with higher baseline densities of total and proliferating (Ki-67+) CD8+ T cells, but independent of CPS and baseline GDF-15 levels in serum and tumor. There were no treatment-related discontinuations or treatment-related delays to surgery; grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in two (13%) and three (20%) patients treated with N + V or N + P, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of visugromab in MIBC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06059547 . As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In this exploratory, nonrandomized phase 2a trial, treatment of patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive muscle-invasive bladder cancer with the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab and nivolumab produced encouraging pathological complete response and radiographic response rates with no new safety signals, supporting further evaluation in larger randomized studies.

title: Warfarin After Seven Decades: Persistent Value and the Contemporary Role of Vitamin K Antagonism
authors: Weverton Ferreira Leite; Wilma Noia Ribeiro; Rui Póvoa; Dirceu Rodrigues Almeida; Daniela Fernanda Alli Hemerly; Bráulio Luna Filho; Valdir Ambrósio Moisés; José Antônio Franchini Ramires
abstract: Warfarin is one of the most enduring drugs in cardiovascular medicine. Although direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have transformed anticoagulation, especially in atrial fibrillation (AF) eligible for DOAC therapy, their success cannot be extrapolated to every thrombotic substrate. This review examines the contemporary boundaries of warfarin and vitamin K antagonist (VKA) therapy. Mechanical heart valves remain the clearest setting in which lifelong international normalized ratio (INR)-guided VKA therapy is required; randomized attempts to substitute dabigatran or apixaban have failed. In rheumatic heart disease-associated AF, INVICTUS favored VKA therapy over rivaroxaban, supporting the VKA class rather than warfarin specifically. High-risk thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome, particularly triple-positive disease, is another VKA-preferred setting. Left ventricular thrombus (LVT) occupies an evolving position in which warfarin remains established, while randomized evidence supports rivaroxaban as a potential alternative in selected acute post-myocardial infarction LVT. Pregnancy with mechanical valves requires dynamic maternal–fetal risk balancing, whereas advanced chronic kidney disease and dialysis represent areas of uncertainty rather than intrinsic indications for warfarin. The global relevance of warfarin also depends on total anticoagulation burden, including INR monitoring, travel, treatment continuity, quality of anticoagulation, and reversal capacity. The persistence of VKA efficacy in selected highly thrombogenic environments raises a biologically plausible hypothesis that broader suppression of vitamin K-dependent factors may matter, but this mechanism is not established by clinical trials. Contemporary anticoagulation should therefore be substrate-centered: VKA therapy remains necessary in some conditions, preferred in others, increasingly replaceable in several, and uncertain in a few.

title: Sudden Cardiac Arrest As the Initial Presentation of Anomalous Left Coronary Artery Originating From the Pulmonary Artery in a Young Adult: A Case Report
authors: Bhupal Shrestha; C Hey; Soon Neoh
abstract: Anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) is a rare congenital heart condition associated with high childhood mortality if untreated.Consequently, diagnosis in asymptomatic adults is exceedingly uncommon.We report a 21-year-old gentleman brought to hospital via the primary percutaneous coronary intervention service after an out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest while hiking.Following prehospital cardiopulmonary resuscitation and defibrillation, return of spontaneous circulation was achieved; an immediate 12-lead electrocardiogram showed ST elevation.Initial transthoracic echocardiography revealed abnormal myocardial color Doppler flow, suggesting intercoronary collaterals and raising suspicion of a coronary anomaly.Coronary angiography confirmed ALCAPA.He underwent successful reimplantation surgery.Given myocardial fibrosis on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention.Sudden cardiac arrest as the initial presenting symptom is exceedingly rare in an asymptomatic young adult with ALCAPA.High clinical suspicion supports early diagnosis.Multi-modality imaging remains central to diagnosis and device-therapy decisions after corrective surgery.

title: Community-Level Wastewater Surveillance of Nicotine Biomarkers Tracks Cardiovascular Disease Burden and Myocardial Infarction
authors: Katherine M. Joseph; Xuan Qin; Katie Clark; Feng Li; Dr. Emily Hartmann; Juan Nañez; Lorissa Humble; Catherine Turlington; John Balliew; Craig K. Cassidy; Jagat Narula; Kristina D. Mena; Fuqing Wu
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tobacco smoking is the largest modifiable contributor to cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet population-level surveillance still relies on self-reported and retail data, which are subject to measuring bias and lag. Urinary and salivary cotinine quantify individual tobacco exposure, but no analogous, objective metric exists at the community level. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has transformed surveillance of infectious diseases and illicit drug use; whether the same approach can yield a community-level signal of CVD risk is unknown. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study is to track community-level wastewater nicotine biomarkers and evaluate potential correlations with relative CVD burden in El Paso, Texas. METHODS: We integrated wastewater nicotine biomarker surveillance with electronic health record (EHR) data across four sewersheds in El Paso, Texas. Twenty-four-hour composite influent samples were collected monthly (June 2024 to May 2025; n=48) and quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry for five nicotine metabolites. Cotinine, nornicotine, and trans-3-hydroxycotinine (3HC) were detected in 91.6 to 100% of samples, whereas tobacco-specific nitrosamines were below limit of detection. CVD cases (January 2021 to December 2024) were obtained from the Paso del Norte Health Information Exchange and mapped to sewersheds by residential ZIP code using ArcGIS. At the sewershed level, population normalized nicotine mass loads tracked the proportional burden of atherosclerosis/ischemia/infarction and heart failure. Across the sewersheds, monthly 3HC mass load and the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR) were strongly and specifically associated with incident ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) (3HC vs. STEMI: rho=0.893,p=0.012), without parallel associations for non-ST elevation or old myocardial infarction. CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that integrating wastewater nicotine surveillance with EHR data can reveal community-level 3HC and NMR as specific indicators of incident STEMI. Our findings indicate wastewater surveillance as a novel, objective tool to inform cessation policy and CVD prevention

title: Prenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Disease by Routine Fetal Echocardiography in Consecutive Pregnancies
authors: A. R. Gayathri; Pulugundla Varun; Sowmya Kasturi; Peddaguravagari Thejaswi; Velam Vanajakshamma
journal: Indian Journal of Cardiovascular Disease in Women
abstract: Objectives: Early prenatal detection of congenital heart disease (CHD) using fetal echocardiography (FE) facilitates comprehensive prenatal evaluation, multidisciplinary perinatal planning, and timely postnatal management, improving outcomes. This study assessed FE for detecting major and complex CHD and identified cases that would have been missed using a risk-based referral strategy. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based prospective observational study was undertaken at a tertiary care teaching institution from June 2023 to January 2024. A total of 120 pregnant women between 15 and 35 weeks of gestation underwent FE irrespective of maternal or fetal risk factors. All live-born neonates underwent postnatal transthoracic echocardiography, which served as the reference standard for diagnostic accuracy. Results: FE detected complex CHD in 11 of the 120 fetuses (9.2%). Of these, nine pregnancies underwent medical termination, whereas two continued to delivery. Postnatal echocardiography was performed in 111 live-born neonates and identified CHD in 22 (19.8%), predominantly minor acyanotic lesions. Compared with the routine screening group, the high-risk group demonstrated a significantly higher detection rate of complex CHD (25.0% vs. 4.3%, p = 0.001). However, routine screening identified four additional cases of complex CHD that would have been missed by high-risk referral alone. FE demonstrated good diagnostic performance for detecting complex CHD, although small ventricular septal defects were not detected prenatally. The number screened to detect one additional case of complex CHD was 23. Conclusion: FE enabled prenatal detection of complex CHD, including additional cases among pregnancies undergoing routine screening without recognized risk factors. These findings support its potential role in prenatal CHD detection.

title: Silent Culprit: Incidental Inferior ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction on Triage Electrocardiogram in an Elderly Man Presenting With Dizziness
authors: David Ramzy; Rouba Isshak; Emile Doss; Yezin F. Shamoon; Abraam Rezkalla; Sacide S. Ozgur; RAYAN SABOUH; Michael Elmasry; Disha Patel; Fady Beshara; Aaryan Patel; Fayez E. Shamoon
abstract: Silent or painless myocardial infarction is well described yet remains a diagnostic challenge, particularly in older adults and those with cognitive impairment, in whom classic anginal symptoms may be absent or difficult to report.We describe an 82-year-old man with hypertension, dyslipidemia, dementia, and coronary artery disease with prior percutaneous coronary intervention who was brought to the emergency department with dizziness and transient lower-extremity weakness after running out of and inconsistently taking his antihypertensive and lipid-lowering medications.He denied chest pain, dyspnea, and diaphoresis.A triage electrocardiogram unexpectedly revealed inferior ST-segment elevation with reciprocal ST-segment depression, prompting activation of a code for ST-elevation myocardial infarction.High-sensitivity troponin levels were markedly elevated.Emergent coronary angiography demonstrated total occlusion of an aneurysmal proximal-to-mid right coronary artery and multivessel disease involving the left coronary system.The culprit lesion was treated with a single drug-eluting stent, restoring normal coronary blood flow, while the residual multivessel disease was managed medically, with planned surgical revascularization.He recovered without hemodynamic compromise.This case underscores that a large, angiographically confirmed infarction may present with only nonspecific symptoms and that a low threshold for early electrocardiography in elderly patients, even those presenting for seemingly unrelated reasons, such as medication refills, can be lifesaving.Recognizing that dementia may mask or hinder communication of ischemic symptoms and addressing lapses in secondary-prevention therapy are essential for timely reperfusion and improved outcomes.

title: PERIOPERATIVE MEDICATION OPTIMIZATION AND EARLY CLINICAL OUTCOMES FOLLOWING TRANSCATHETER AORTIC VALVE REPLACEMENT IN SEVERE AORTIC STENOSIS: A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL COHORT STUDY
authors: Syed Fozail Sarmad; Javeria Javed; Dr. Asad Ullah; Dr. Muhammad Mubashir Rasheed; Muhammad Mubashir Rasheed
journal: Review journal of neurological & medical sciences review.
abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has become the treatment of choice for patients with high-risk or elderly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis (AS) [1]. However, the complexity of the patients' multi-morbidities and their extensive therapy poses an enormous challenge for peri-interventional pharmacotherapy [16]. This prospective observational cohort study aimed to investigate the prevalence of relevant peri-interventional medication discrepancies and their impact on 30-day outcomes following TAVR in tertiary care cardiovascular hospitals in Rawalpindi, Pakistan [17]. Methods: We prospectively enrolled 120 consecutive adult patients undergoing elective TAVR. Comprehensive standardized multi-disciplinary medication reconciliation was performed at four perioperative milestones: admission, pre-procedure, discharge and 30-day follow up [16]. Patients were divided into two groups based on the presence of any periprocedural medication optimization: those with at least one clinically significant medication discrepancy or non-indication based treatment departure vs those receiving fully optimized pharmacotherapy. The primary endpoint was a 30-day composite clinical endpoint including clinically relevant bleeding (Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 [VARC-3] criteria) [5], acute kidney injury (AKIN/KDIGO criteria) [14], stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA), symptomatic hypotension requiring vasopressor/inotropic support, unplanned 30-day cardiac readmissions [15] and all-cause mortality. Results: Out of 120 study participants (mean age: 73.4 ± 6.2 years; 43.3% female), 38 patients (31.7%) had at least one clinically significant medication discrepancy while 82 patients (68.3%) underwent fully optimized pharmacotherapy. The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 of the total patients (23.3%). Patients in the medication discrepancy group had a substantially higher incidence of 30-day composite adverse events than patients in the optimized pharmacotherapy group (42.1% vs. 14.6%; Odds Ratio [OR]: 4.23, 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.76 to 10.18, p < 0.001). Specifically, higher rates of acute kidney injury (18.4% vs. 4.9%; p = 0.024), and 30-day unplanned hospital readmissions (21.1% vs. 6.1%; p = 0.019) were observed in the medication discrepancy group. Perioperative medication discrepancy was independently associated with 30-day composite adverse outcomes as demonstrated by multivariable logistic regression analysis (adjusted OR: 3.64, 95% CI: 1.42 to 9.32, p = 0.007). Conclusion: Perioperative medication discrepancies are highly prevalent among TAVR candidates in South Asian clinical practice and significantly increase early morbidity and unplanned hospital readmissions [17]. Systematic clinical pharmacy-led medication reconciliation and strict adherence to indication-based antithrombotic guidelines represent essential strategies to optimize periprocedural safety and enhance post-TAVR recovery [16].

title: Neuronal intermediate filament neurologic autoimmunity in a patient with Merkel cell carcinoma receiving pembrolizumab
authors: Ali Hijazi; Saffet Guleryuz; Mark Andrew Walshauser; Ghazala R. Hayat; Maithreyi Chappidi
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neuronal intermediate filament (NIF) autoimmunity is an uncommon paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome that has increasingly been recognized in association with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Merkel cell carcinoma is among the malignancies most frequently associated with NIF antibodies, although reported cases remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old female with stage IIIA Merkel cell carcinoma developed vertigo, gait instability, dysarthria, and persistent right hemifacial and cervical spasms after receiving second dose of pembrolizumab for recurrent disease. Brain MRI was unremarkable, while continuous electroencephalography demonstrated encephalopathy without a definitive electrocerebral correlate, raising suspicion for subcortical myoclonus. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein. CSF and positive NIF antibodies using cell-based assay. Pembrolizumab was discontinued, and the patient was treated with high-dose corticosteroids followed by monthly intravenous immunoglobulin, resulting in near complete resolution of her neurologic symptoms after 6 months. CONCLUSION: This case expands the growing spectrum of ICI-associated NIF paraneoplastic neurologic autoimmunity complicating Merkel cell carcinoma. To our knowledge, persistent hemifacial and cervical spasm has rarely been reported in this clinical setting. Early recognition of this syndrome, prompt antibody testing, discontinuation of ICI therapy, and initiation of therapy may improve neurological outcomes while informing further oncologic management.

title: [Clinical characteristics and prognosis of patients with atrial functional mitral regurgitation].
authors: P W Wang; M H Lin; Y L Wei; Y M Liu; S X Zheng; J F Wang; Q Qiu
abstract: Compared with VFMR, AFMR is more common among elderly patients, female patients, and patients with atrial fibrillation and is less frequently accompanied by heart failure symptoms. The rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure are both lower in the AFMR group than those in the VFMR group.

authors: Dinesh Kumar Sathanantham; Jayakumar Thanathu Krishnan Nair; Manjusha N. Pillai; Shiva Ramaratnam; Joseph Thomas Kathayanat; Nidheesh Chooriyil

title: Comparative Evaluation of Reasoning Consistency Detection Methods on LLM Outputs in Cardiovascular Clinical Scenarios
authors: Hairatunnisa; Herman Herman; Muhammad Kunta Biddinika
journal: BULLETIN OF NETWORK ENGINEER AND INFORMATICS
abstract: The advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) presents opportunities for developing cognitive assistants in the medical field, particularly in cardiovascular care.However, hallucinations and reasoning inconsistencies remain significant challenges, while the evaluation of logical consistency in this domain is limited due to the absence of public datasets with clear ground truth. This study aims to compare the effectiveness of Self-Consistency (LLM), Sentiment Heuristic, and Keyword Overlap methods in detecting reasoning inconsistencies using a synthetic dataset of 90 cardiovascular clinical scenarios (30 scenarios with 3 variants each). Performance was evaluated based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, and benchmarked against a fine-tuning approach. The results show that the zero-shot detector based on self-consistency achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 97.78% and an F1-score of 98.31%, while the fine-tuning approach on the limited synthetic dataset failed to surpass these results. These findings indicate that the semantic reasoning capabilities of LLMs have the potential to serve as consistency detectors without additional training, and can serve as a foundation for developing cognitive assistant systems in the cardiovascular domain.

title: Guide-sheath-assisted bailout technique for intra-procedural single-leaflet device attachment using the PASCAL system: a case report
authors: M Nukariya; Yuki Nishimura; Yoko Nakaoka; Kazuya Kawai; Hiroki Sugane
abstract: Abstract Background Single-leaflet device attachment（SLDA）is a rare but serious complication of mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair（MTEER）. When SLDA occurs after full device release, management options are limited. In contrast, intra-procedural SLDA recognized before full implant release may allow a specific bailout strategy. Case summary A 77-year-old man with severe degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR) underwent MTEER using the PASCAL Ace system because of high surgical risk. Initial device implantation reduced MR from severe to mild. However, after removal of both clasp lines during the release process, SLDA occurred at the posterior leaflet, resulting in recurrent severe MR. Although standard retrieval was no longer feasible, the implant remained connected to the steerable catheter. Under fluoroscopic and transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, a guide sheath was advanced coaxially toward the implant. Controlled insertion of the guide sheath between the clasp and paddle, followed by gradual paddle opening, enabled leaflet disengagement and successful device retrieval without leaflet injury. A second implantation achieved a sufficient reduction in mitral regurgitation. Discussion This case demonstrates a novel bailout technique for intra-procedural SLDA. Successful retrieval requires precise coaxial device alignment, careful catheter manipulation, continuous monitoring of leaflet tension, and meticulous guidance using fluoroscopy and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). Importantly, prompt recognition of SLDA by TEE is a prerequisite of this technique. In conclusion, the guide-sheath-assisted retrieval technique can represent a potential bailout strategy for intra-procedural SLDA before full implant release during MTEER.

title: Generalised alopecia caused by iatrogenic supplementation of estriol for treatment of urinary incontinence in a 13‐year‐old, spayed, female miniature poodle
authors: Brenda L. Mulherin; Olivia Stricklin; Jame O. Noxon
abstract: Abstract Urinary incontinence is a disorder associated with involuntary leakage of urine. Multiple estrogenic compounds have been used to manage urinary incontinence. While treatment for urinary incontinence will undoubtedly improve the quality of life for both the owner and the pet, it is not without potential side effects. It is extremely important to discuss proper administration of any medication to be administered to a patient and discuss the potential side effects that can manifest with supplementation or over‐supplementation. This case report describes a 13‐year‐old, spayed, female miniature poodle that developed alopecia along the dorsal thoracolumbar region and hindlimbs caused by iatrogenic supplementation of estriol for treatment of urinary incontinence.

title: Clinically Actionable Prevention and Management of Major Complications During Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Support: A Contemporary Narrative Review
authors: Yong Wei; Tian Sheng Tang; You Shi Wu; Hussain Asif; ZAKARIA SAIFANE; Da Fa Zhang
abstract: Durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) have become an established therapy for selected patients with advanced heart failure as bridge-to-transplant or destination therapy. Despite major progress in continuous-flow pump design and perioperative care, long-term benefit remains constrained by a recurrent burden of right heart failure, aortic regurgitation, pump thrombosis, stroke, bleeding, infection, and end-organ dysfunction. Because these events often arise from the interaction of altered hemodynamics, hemocompatibility-related injury, chronic antithrombotic exposure, and the practical complexity of longitudinal device care, a complication-centered management framework is clinically useful. This contemporary narrative review focuses on actionable prevention, surveillance, and treatment strategies for the major complications encountered during durable LVAD support. Rather than providing a broad device-oriented overview, we emphasize clinically relevant decision points across the perioperative and long-term course, including right ventricular protection, antithrombotic balance, structured monitoring for aortic regurgitation and hemolysis, prevention of driveline infection, and multidisciplinary outpatient follow-up. By organizing current evidence around practical management pathways, this review aims to support earlier recognition of adverse events and more durable long-term support.

title: Collagen and myocyte interplay in cardiac volume overload: a multi-constituent growth and remodeling framework
authors: L. Maga; Mathias Peirlinck; L. Noël
abstract: Abstract Hearts subjected to volume overload (VO) are prone to detrimental anatomical and functional changes in response to elevated mechanical loading, ultimately leading to heart failure. Experimental findings now emphasize that organ-scale changes following VO cannot be explained by myocyte growth alone, as traditionally proposed in the literature. Collagen degradation, in particular, has been associated with VO and assumed to play a central role in both its acute and chronic stages. This hypothesis, however, remains to be substantiated by comprehensive mechanistic evidence, and each constituent contribution to myocardial growth and remodeling (G&R) processes is yet to be quantified. In this work, we present a multi-constituent G&R framework that integrates a mixture-based constitutive model within the kinematic growth formulation. This framework enables us to mechanistically assess the relative contributions of collagen and myocyte changes to alterations in tissue properties, ventricular dimensions, and growth phenotype. Our numerical results confirm that collagen remodeling affects the passive mechanical response of the myocardium, whereas myocytes predominantly influence the extent and phenotype of VO-induced growth. Importantly, collagen degradation exacerbates myocyte hypertrophy, revealing a synergistic interplay that accelerates the left ventricular eccentric growth and thereby promotes systolic dysfunction. This work constitutes an important step towards an integrated characterization of the early compensatory stages of VO-induced cardiac G&R.

title: Mitral regurgitation and left atrial phasic function and atrioventricular coupling in patients with myocardial infarction: a cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study
authors: Xiaoling Wen; Guo Ying-kun; Yue Gao; Zhi-Gang Yang
journal: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery
abstract: Background: Mitral regurgitation (MR) after myocardial infarction (MI) may increase left atrial (LA) pressure and contribute to cardiac dysfunction. This study evaluated the incremental association of MR with LA phasic function and strain and identified independent factors associated with LA deformation in patients with MI. Methods: This retrospective study included 189 patients with MI (111 without MR and 78 with MR: mild, 27; moderate, 33; severe, 18) and 86 normal controls who underwent 3.0-T cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). MR severity was graded by the CMR-derived MR fraction: mild <30%, moderate 30% to <50%, and severe ≥50%. CMR-derived LA phasic function and strain (reservoir strain, epsilon-s; booster strain, epsilon-a; conduit strain, epsilon-e), left ventricular (LV) function and strain, infarct size, and MR fraction were measured. Between-group comparisons were performed using one-way analysis of variance or the Kruskal-Wallis test with post hoc correction, and multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent factors associated with LA strain. A two-sided P<0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Patients with MI and MR had lower LA reservoir strains [22.14%±10.91% vs. 28.65% (22.78%, 38.30%) vs. 41.70% (36.15%, 53.15%)], booster strains [11.52%±6.19% vs. 13.80% (10.20%, 19.80%) vs. 19.25% (15.10%, 24.05%)], and conduit strains [9.40% (6.03%, 14.85%) vs. 14.60% (9.60%, 20.50%) vs. 22.55% (17.75%, 30.43%)] than patients with MI without MR and controls (all P<0.05). They also had higher LA maximum volume [68.43 (57.44, 91.51) mL] and minimum volume [35.93 (24.43, 61.15) mL] and lower LA total ejection fraction (45.39%±14.97%) than the other groups (all P<0.05). In multivariable analysis, MR degree was independently associated with reservoir strain (β=−0.194, P=0.048) and conduit strain (β=−0.208, P=0.038). Anterior wall MI (reservoir strain: β=−0.245, P=0.014; booster strain: β=−0.231, P=0.028; conduit strain: β=−0.224, P=0.027) and posteromedial papillary muscle infarction (reservoir strain: β=−0.329, P=0.004; booster strain: β=−0.370, P=0.003) were also independently associated with LA strain. Conclusions: MR was associated with further deterioration of LA myocardial strain in patients with MI. Posteromedial papillary muscle infarction, anterior wall MI, beta-blocker use, and dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin plus clopidogrel were independently associated with LA strain. CMR-derived functional and strain parameters may help characterize LV-LA coupling and support risk stratification in this population.

title: Acute Changes in Left Atrial Appendage Flow Velocity During Pulsed Field Ablation: An Intraprocedural Intracardiac Echocardiography Study
authors: Yu Pan; Pavel P. Osmancik; Tomas Knize; Josef Hornof; Dalibor Heřman; Sabri Hassouna; Erika Slusnakova; Stepan Soukup; Marek Hozman
abstract: **Background:** Despite the close anatomical relationship between the left pulmonary veins (PVs) and the left atrial appendage (LAA), acute changes in LAA flow during pulsed field ablation (PFA) remain poorly characterized. **Objectives:** To characterize acute intraprocedural changes in LAA flow and transmitral filling during PFA for atrial fibrillation (AF) using paired intracardiac echocardiography (ICE). **Methods:** Patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing PFA were prospectively enrolled if they were in sinus rhythm at the beginning of the procedure. ICE was performed immediately before and after PFA to assess LAA emptying velocity (LAAEv), LAA filling velocity (LAAFv), transmitral E- and A-wave velocities, and E-wave deceleration time (EDT). Paired pre-to-post PFA changes were assessed, followed by a sensitivity analysis using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) and exploratory subgroup analyses. **Results:** Among 98 patients, LAAEv increased from 35.45 to 40.00 cm/s immediately after PFA (estimated paired increase, 4.95 cm/s; 95% CI, 2.35-7.80; P less than 0.001), while LAAFv increased by 4.36 cm/s (95% CI, 1.81-6.91; P=0.001). E-wave velocity increased by 8.69 cm/s and EDT decreased by 31.73 ms (both P less than 0.001), whereas A-wave velocity did not change significantly (P=0.08). In the ANCOVA model, changes in heart rate, systolic blood pressure, and vasopressor use were not significantly associated with changes in LAAEv. A marked acute reduction in LAAEv (20% or greater) occurred in 12 patients (12.2%). No significant subgroup interactions were observed. **Conclusions:** LAA flow velocities increased acutely after PFA, accompanied by changes in transmitral filling, although a minority of patients showed a marked acute reduction in LAA emptying.

title: Exercise Echocardiography in the Diagnostic Work-up of Unexplained Dyspnoea: A Critical Narrative Review of Physiological Targets, Diagnostic Performance and Unresolved Controversies
authors: Malki Mohamed; Loudiyi Nadia; Lakhal Zouhair; Benyass Aatif
journal: Asian Journal of Research in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
abstract: Background: Chronic exertional dyspnoea frequently remains unexplained after clinical assessment, natriuretic peptide measurement and resting echocardiography. Many underlying cardiovascular abnormalities, particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and exercise pulmonary hypertension, become apparent only during physiological stress. Exercise echocardiography is non-invasive, widely available and free of ionising radiation, but its diagnostic role outside ischaemia testing remains contested. Purpose and Scope: This critical narrative review evaluates the evidence supporting exercise echocardiography in adults with chronic exertional dyspnoea that remains unexplained after first-line evaluation. It examines test conduct and feasibility, the diastolic stress test, pulmonary vascular and right ventricular responses, ischaemic, valvular and dynamic obstructive causes, and multiparametric approaches incorporating lung ultrasound, cardiopulmonary exercise testing and artificial intelligence. Methods: Literature was identified through structured searches of bibliographic databases and scholarly indexes, supplemented by citation tracking and professional-society guidance. Evidence was appraised with attention to patient spectrum, reference standards, feasibility reporting and outcome relevance, and synthesised thematically. Principal Findings: Invasive studies consistently show that exercise unmasks haemodynamic abnormalities that resting tests miss. Exercise-derived echocardiographic abnormalities, including elevated filling-pressure surrogates, exercise pulmonary hypertension and exercise-induced pulmonary congestion, carry consistent prognostic information. The diagnostic accuracy of individual markers, especially the ratio of early mitral inflow to early diastolic annular velocity, is considerably less secure: validation studies conflict, largely because of differences in patient spectrum, reference standards and measurement timing. Tricuspid regurgitation signals are frequently unobtainable at peak exercise, and the incremental value of stress testing over probability scores appears modest in several invasive validation cohorts. Left atrial mechanics, systolic reserve, cardiac output-indexed pulmonary pressures and lung ultrasound show promise but require external validation. Unresolved Questions: Consensus is lacking on the reference standard, age- and sex-specific normal responses, optimal protocols and the effect of test-guided management on patient outcomes. Implications and Conclusion: Exercise echocardiography is best regarded as a question-driven, multiparametric physiological test integrated with pre-test probability and, where available, gas-exchange measurement, rather than as a single-parameter rule-in or rule-out tool. Prospective multicentre studies with invasive reference standards and outcome-oriented diagnostic trials are needed before stronger recommendations can be justified.

title: Cardiorespiratory Arrest in the Context of Graves' Disease: A Rare Presentation
authors: Mariana Marques; Joana Couto; Madalena Martins Vale; Pedro Pinto; Paula Felgueiras
abstract: Thyroid storm is the most severe and life-threatening expression of thyrotoxicosis, and its diagnosis remains clinical.Although sinus tachycardia and atrial fibrillation dominate its cardiovascular manifestations, malignant ventricular arrhythmias are rare, and cardiorespiratory arrest as the presenting manifestation of Graves' disease has been reported only in a limited number of cases.We report the case of a 44-year-old man with a one-week history of symptoms consistent with hyperthyroidism who suffered a witnessed out-of-hospital cardiorespiratory arrest with ventricular fibrillation as the initial rhythm.Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved after three defibrillations, and urgent coronary angiography showed no obstructive coronary artery disease.Laboratory evaluation revealed severe thyrotoxicosis with positive thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)-receptor antibodies, and thyroid ultrasound findings supported the diagnosis of Graves' disease.Thyroid storm was suspected and treated empirically, but the diagnosis could not be confirmed: the Burch-Wartofsky score reached the diagnostic threshold only when post-arrest coma was included, and the Japan Thyroid Association criteria were not met.Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and an ajmaline provocation test did not identify structural heart disease, myocarditis, or a Brugada pattern.Thyroid hormone excess was therefore considered the most likely precipitant of the arrhythmia, although causality cannot be proven.The patient was maintained on antithyroid therapy, and a subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention following an individualized risk-benefit assessment.This case highlights the importance of considering thyrotoxicosis in the etiological workup of unexplained cardiac arrest.When a clearly established and reversible cause of the arrhythmia cannot be confirmed, management, including the decision on defibrillator implantation, should be based on an individualized risk-benefit assessment.

title: Prevalence of Structural Heart Disease Detected By Echocardiography among Adults Living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus on Antiretroviral Therapy in Eastern Nepal
authors: Supriya Mishra; Dr Prashant Shah
journal: International Journal of Medical Sciences and Academic Research
abstract: Background: Improved survival on antiretroviral therapy has shifted morbidity in human immunodeficiency virus infection towards non-communicable cardiac disease, yet echocardiographic data from South Asia remain sparse. Aims/Objectives: To determine the prevalence of structural heart disease, comprising dilated cardiomyopathy and valvular heart disease, and its association with age, sex and CD4 count. Methodology: A hospital-based cross-sectional study enrolled 126 consecutive adults on antiretroviral therapy at a tertiary centre in eastern Nepal between August 2018 and July 2019. Those with hypertension, alcohol dependence, cardiotoxic drug exposure or pre-existing cardiac or systemic disease were excluded. All underwent transthoracic echocardiography and CD4 estimation. Results: Structural heart disease was present in 19 (15.1%) participants: dilated cardiomyopathy in 14 (11.1%) and valvular heart disease in 7 (5.6%). Prevalence did not differ across age groups (χ² = 0.94, p = 0.627) or by sex (11/64 men, 17.2%, versus 8/62 women, 12.9%; odds ratio 1.40, 95% CI 0.52–3.76, p = 0.502). Mean CD4 count was similar in affected and unaffected participants (627 ± 309 versus 551 ± 248 cells/µL; t = 1.18, p = 0.239). Conclusions: One in seven treated adults had unsuspected structural heart disease, independent of age, sex and CD4 count, supporting routine echocardiographic screening.

title: Association between autoimmune diseases and risk of developing breast cancer-related lymphedema
authors: Benjamin D. Wagner; Stav Brown; Andrea Veronica Barrio; Thomas Amburn; Natália Polidorio; Tiana Le; Lilian Boe; Raghu P. Kataru; Geoffrey E. Hespe; Michelle R Coriddi; Danielle H. Rochlin; Hidehiko Yoshimatsu; Babak Joseph Mehrara
abstract: Abstract Preexisting autoimmune disease may increase susceptibility to breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL) through chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, but its association with BCRL risk is poorly understood. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing sentinel lymph node biopsy and/or axillary lymph node dissection for breast cancer at a tertiary cancer center between 2010 and 2021. Autoimmune diseases were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-9/10 codes, and the primary outcome was BCRL diagnosis based on ICD codes. Associations between autoimmune disease and time to BCRL were evaluated using univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Among 20,027 patients with a median follow-up of 61.7 months (IQR, 38.7–94.2), 1361 (6.8%) had a preexisting autoimmune disease and 1728 (8.6%) developed BCRL at a median of 17.4 months (IQR, 8.0–33.9) after surgery. In multivariable analysis, autoimmune disease was independently associated with increased BCRL risk (hazard ratio [HR], 1.52; 95% CI, 1.30–1.77; P < .001). Elevated risks were observed for rheumatoid arthritis (HR, 1.54), autoimmune thyroiditis (HR, 1.40), Graves’ disease (HR, 1.49), multiple sclerosis (HR, 1.87), systemic lupus erythematosus (HR, 2.46), and systemic sclerosis (HR, 2.10). These findings suggest autoimmune disease may be an independent risk factor for BCRL and may improve risk stratification.

title: ECG-Derived Synthetic Left Ventricular Mechanics Predict Mortality After Acute Myocardial Infarction and Fatal Myocardial Infarction in the General Population
authors: Douglas Robert Corsi; John Furst; Ankush D. Jamthikar; Sajeev Singh; Gabriela M M Paixao; Antonio Ribeiro; Jagat Narula; BERNARD R. CHAITMAN; Jeffrey L. Carson; Naveena V. K. Yanamala; Partho P. Sengupta
abstract: Background: Left ventricular (LV) mechanical function predicts outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Recovering these parameters from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) could enable point-of-care risk assessment wherever an ECG is acquired. Objectives: To determine whether ECG-derived synthetic LV mechanics predict all-cause mortality after AMI and myocardial infarction (MI)-specific mortality in the general population and add information beyond the GRACE score and ejection fraction. Methods: Synthetic peak systolic (s′) and early diastolic (e′) mitral annular velocities and mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) were derived from the 12-lead ECG by a previously validated generative adversarial network, applied without retraining and blinded to outcome. Associations were assessed in an AMI cohort (n=1,065) by Cox regression and a population cohort (n=219,564) by Fine-Gray models. Incremental value was tested against GRACE, three AI-ECG reduced ejection fraction (EF) models, and measured LVEF. Results: In the AMI cohort (109 deaths; median follow-up 1.44 years), all three parameters predicted all-cause mortality (each P<0.001). Synthetic e′ was the sole independent predictor after adjustment for clinical covariates (HR=0.90 per 1 cm/s; 95% CI 0.84-0.98) and for GRACE (HR=0.90; 0.83-0.97; P=0.006). In the post-discharge cohort (n=1,017; 61 deaths), synthetic e′ improved discrimination beyond GRACE (C-index 0.67 to 0.70; HR=0.84 per 1 cm/s; 95% CI 0.76-0.93; P=0.001) and remained independent of AI-ECG-predicted and measured LVEF (HR 0.84-0.86 per 1 cm/s; all P≤0.004), contributing 28-46% of each model's prognostic information. In the population cohort (817 MI deaths; median follow-up 3.42 years), all three predicted MI-specific mortality after adjustment for age, sex, and ECG abnormalities, MAPSE showing the largest effect (sHR=0.49; 95% CI 0.37-0.65), with s′ (sHR=0.78; 0.72-0.84) and e′ (sHR=0.87; 0.82-0.93) also predictive (each P<0.001). Conclusions: ECG-derived synthetic LV mechanical parameters predict all-cause mortality after AMI and fatal MI in the general population, adding information beyond the GRACE score and LVEF. Keywords: electrocardiogram; tissue Doppler imaging; generative adversarial network; myocardial infarction; mortality prediction; risk stratification.

title: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number and Mitochondrial Homeostasis Genes in Acute and Stable Coronary Artery Disease
authors: Paola Canale; Jonica Campolo; Marina Parolini; Cinzia Dellanoce; Emanuela Piccaluga; Irene Maria Bossi; Matteo Maurina; Jacopo Oreglia; Rosa Sicari; Maria Grazia Andreassi
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in coronary artery disease (CAD), but the relationship between mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtDNA-CN) and mitochondrial homeostasis across CAD presentations remains unclear. We investigated mtDNA-CN together with the expression of key regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α and TFAM) and mitophagy (PINK1) in patients with stable angina (SA) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). METHODS: This observational study included 334 patients: 170 ACS, 117 SA and 47 individuals with non-obstructive coronary arteries (NCA). Peripheral blood mtDNA-CN and the expression of PGC-1α, TFAM and PINK1 were quantified by real-time PCR. Associations with clinical characteristics, inflammatory markers and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were evaluated. RESULTS: ACS patients exhibited significantly lower mtDNA-CN than SA and NCA groups (p = 0.01 and p = 0.004, respectively). PINK1 expression was reduced in both ACS (p = 0.005) and SA (p = 0.01) compared with NCA. TFAM expression was increased in SA (p = 0.009), while PGC-1α expression was higher in ACS (p = 0.02). MtDNA-CN and mitochondrial biomarkers were inversely associated with inflammatory markers, whereas mtDNA-CN and TFAM correlated positively with LVEF. Lower mtDNA-CN was independently associated with ACS (OR = 0.98, p = 0.0004) and SA (OR = 0.99, p = 0.04), while higher PINK1 expression was associated with reduced odds of SA (p = 0.03) and ACS (p = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: Mitochondrial markers are altered across CAD phenotypes. ACS is characterized by lower mtDNA-CN and altered expression of mitochondrial homeostasis-related genes, whereas SA shows a pattern consistent with a possible compensatory response. Combined assessment of mtDNA-CN and mitochondrial homeostasis-related gene expression may provide a novel biomarker strategy for CAD risk stratification and targeted therapies. TRIAL REGISTRATION: VICTORIA study, (ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06313645).
